trickyParts: Four rounds, five defects, one class: a sentence nobody had run or opened sitting beside sentences someone had. Two were the architect's by instruction (df -x, and df ~/.cache saying nothing about the budget), one a citation that named the wrong container, one an inherited mechanism this change never ran, and one an instrument claim that was true of du -x and false of du. Every one was caught by running the command or opening the record, and none by reading the prose. That is the finding this issue should leave behind, and it belongs in retro.

A note cannot cite a Legion handoff: retro deletes .legion/<issue>/ before the merge, so a figure whose only home is implement.json becomes unopenable the moment the change lands. Anything a reader must be able to check belongs in the pull request body, which survives as main's commit message, or in a Dispatch record.
